newsitem.title: SHARJAH: CRICKET-PROLIFIC DE SILVA INSPIRES SRI LANKA TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PROLIFIC DE SILVA INSPIRES SRI LANKA TRIUMPH.

text.p: Aravinda de Silva left an indelible mark on the Sharjah Cup with another high-quality innings as Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by four wickets in the final of the $75,000 tournament on Friday.

De Silva crowned his prolific form in the three-nation event with an unbeaten 87 off 124 balls to spur Sri Lanka home at 215 for six with four balls left after they dismissed Pakistan for 214 in 49.2 of their 50 overs.
With a total of 410 runs in five innings at an average of 136.66, de Silva was named Man of the Series, underlining the significance of his role for the World Cup champions in the final run chase.

De Silva, who hit only three fours, first put on 66 off 94 balls for the fourth wicket with skipper Arjuna Ranatunga (28 from 41 balls) and then added 60 in 91 balls for the fifth wicket with Roshan Mahanama (31 off 51 balls).
The tournament victory, Sri Lanka's first in Sharjah since October 1995, was worth $40,000 while Pakistan received $25,000 as runners up. Zimbabwe, who failed to qualify for ther final, got $10,000.
Earlier, solid half-centuries from Inzamam-ul-Haq (61) and Salim Malik (58) provided middle order substance to Pakistan's innings after they opted to bat on winning the toss.
However, after reaching 185 for three in 43 overs, Pakistan's last seven wickets crashed for 29 in 6.1 overs.
Backed by a vociferous crowd, Inzamam scored his runs off 75 balls with two fours and a six while Malik faced 76 balls and struck three fours. They put on 98 from 108 deliveries balls.
The lower order, trying desperately to step up the scoring rate in the final overs, squandered wickets in the face of nagging bowling, backed by a smart fielding.
Off-spinner Muttiah Muralitharan took three for 42 in his 10 overs, with pace bowlers Chaminda Vaas and Sajeeva de Silva taking two wickets each.
Pakistan skipper Wasim Akram paid tribute to the fighting qualities of the Sri Lankans. "They played really well, but Aravinda made all the difference," he said.

Ranatunga said: "We had a point to prove after a bad tour of New Zealand. Our performance here underlines our capabilities as one-day world champions. We beat Pakistan three times in 10 days, which is not a joke. It all happened because of Aravinda."
